To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) PH induces a genome-wide increase in liver histone acetylation, 2) Zn-HDAC activity is required to maintain this PH-induced hyperacetylation, and 3) the PH-induced increase in liver histones H3 and H4 acetylation is associated with increased expression of pro-regenerative genes and decreased expression of anti-regenerative genes.

the epigenetic regulation of liver regeneration is characterized by hyperacetylation and deacetylations of genes involved in liver regeneration and that the Zn-HDACi SAHA disrupts the epigenetic signature associated with liver regeneration.

we have identified a genome-wide epigenetic signature for liver regeneration that includes hyperacetylation (activation) of pro-regenerative genes and deacetylations (suppression) of anti-proliver regenerative factors, and that administration of the Zn-HDAI inhibitor SAHA disrupts the pro-regenerative changes that occur in histone acetylation during early liver regeneration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate the regenerative response of the liver to injury.
the identification of novel mechanisms that regulate liver regenerative capacity and the development of strategies that may be useful in improving liver disease outcomes.
the epigenetic regulation of liver regeneration and how such processes are disrupted in liver disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our data provide the first description of a genome-wide epigenetic signature for liver regeneration that is regulated by Zn-HDACs and that such Zn-HDAC activity is essential to maintain the regenerative response during the early phases of liver regeneration.
the results of this study provide new insight into the epigenetic regulation of liver regeneration.

the data presented herein provide new insights into the epigenetic control of early liver regeneration and identify an epigenetic profile that is disrupted during impaired regeneration induced by Zn-HDAC inhibitor SAHA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the epigenetic signature that is associated with the early regenerative response to PH includes both hyperacetylating and deacetylating events, and Zn-HDAC inhibition disrupts the epigenetic changes that are associated with PH-induced regeneration.
the epigenetic signature that is established in the liver during early regeneration after PH is disrupted by ZnHDAc inhibition.
the histone acetyl signature that is established in the liver following PH is disrupted by Zn-dependent histone deactivase inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
epigenetic mechanisms play a critical role in regulating the liver's response to partial hepactectomy.
the epigenome changes in response to liver injury and regeneration, and that this response is disrupted when Zn-HDAC activity is inhibited.
the histone acetyltransferase (HAT) activity of p300 is required for the induction of pro-regenerative gene expression in response to partial (PH) or complete (CL) hepatectomy.
